Tube EQ: A broad musical EQ curve into warm tube saturation, like a vintage tube equalizer.
Reverse Reverb: A big reverb played backwards, so sounds swell in before they hit.
Lo-Fi: Grit, worn vinyl and a dark low-pass for a dusty, sampled sound.
Cassette: Tape saturation, wow, flutter and hiss with a gentle top-end roll-off.
Lo-Fi Echo: A filtered, driven delay into grit, like an old tape echo.
Bass Enhancer: Adds a sub octave and warmth, then keeps the low end mono.
Drum Bus: Punchier transients, tape warmth and glue compression for a drum group.
Ensemble: Chorus, doubling and spread for a wide, lush stereo image.
Guitar Amp: Gate, crunchy amp, 4x12 cabinet and a touch of room for DI guitar.
Bass Amp: Bass amp, 1x15 cabinet and steady compression for DI bass.
Vocal Chain: Gate, breath control, de-essing, compression, EQ, doubling and reverb in the usual order.
Dialogue Cleanup: Removes hum and noise, tames sibilance, evens out the level and catches peaks.
Mastering Chain: Clean-up EQ, multiband compression, width, a maximizer and a loudness meter.
Multiband Distortion: Three saturation stages on the lows, mids and highs, each with its own character.
Multiband Width: Mono lows, a wider midrange and the widest highs, split by Band Splitter.
Dynamic Width: The stereo image opens up as the music gets louder.
Mid/Side EQ: One EQ for the center and another for the sides.
Auto Filter: A resonant low-pass swept by an LFO.
Ducked Delay: A ping-pong delay that steps back while you play and blooms in the gaps.
Build-Up: One control raises the riser, the filter sweep and the pumping together for an EDM build-up.
Lo-Fi Fader: One control fades in grit and worn vinyl while closing the low-pass.
Six-Fader Vocal: Bass, treble, compression, reverb, delay and doubling for vocals, each on its own control and all starting closed.
Vocal Leveler: Breath control, slow leveling, de-essing, resonance and mud control with a little air: vocal level and tone, no effects.
Harmony Stack: Gentle pitch correction, a third and a fifth above, doubling, width and a hall; one control brings the voices up.
Robot Radio Voice: Hard-tuned robot voice through a moving vowel filter, a narrow band-pass, tube drive and a spring.
VHS Tape: Tape heat, chorus, slow pitch drift, crushing and a dark wash, each on its own control, for a worn videotape sound.
Old Radio: Mono, a narrow band, tube drive, crackle and a little spring, with a low-pass that drifts like a weak signal.
Sit-in-Mix: Light compression, tape warmth and a slight tilt to help a track sit in the mix; one control does more of both.
Mix Bus Finisher: High-pass, glue, gentle multiband, a push EQ, wider highs, mono lows, a touch of OTT and a limiter for a mix bus.
Small Speaker Check: Mono, band-limited and mid-forward: hear the mix as a phone or small speaker would. Bypass it before rendering.
Kick Fertilizer: Kick shaping, a sub octave and a burst of noise in the highs that follows each hit, then punch and a limiter.
Fragment Gate: A 16th-note gate into a randomly stepping band-pass, synced panning, octave blips, an eighth-note delay and some room.
Stepped Autopan: Tempo pumping and synced panning into a band-pass that jumps between two steps every half note.
Funk Rig: Touch-wah or phaser into a clean amp, combo cabinet and spring, for clavinet, keys and funk guitar.
Organ Rotary: Tube drive into a rotary speaker and a small room; one control switches from slow to fast.
Broken Media: Digital breakage (crushing, stutters) on one control and analog wear (wobble, crackle) on another.
Mid/Side Drive: A drifting comb, tube drive on the center and crunch on the sides that grows with the input level.
Color Drive: A movable bell boost before tube drive, crunch on the highs, a tilt and a short Haas widening.
Tube Smash: Fast compression into tube saturation, with controls for low-end weight and drive.
Shift Mod: A slowly drifting frequency shift on the sides, optional ring modulation, a wide band-pass and extra width.
Triple Mod: Phaser, flanger on the sides and chorus with drifting rate and depth, plus slow panning; one control adds all three.
Distorted Throw: A driven ping-pong delay into tape saturation and a resonant low-pass that sweeps every two bars.
Harshness Tamer: Resonance suppression, a dynamic cut at 3.5 kHz, de-essing and a darker tilt; one control smooths more.
Cosmic Space: A drifting metallic comb, granular echoes and a huge reverb, with a freeze that holds the sound.
Wide Lift: Excitement, a little sub, extra width and loudness for a bigger, more open sound; Amount does more of all of it, Air brightens the top.
Motion Pad: Lush chorus, a slowly breathing low-pass, synced panning and a shimmer tail for pads; Amount adds motion and space, Speed moves it faster.
Retro Bus: Chorus, tape and a dark dotted-eighth echo into a small room; Amount brings the effects up, Age adds wobble, hiss and a duller echo.
Micro Grains: Short granular echoes, reversed snippets and stutters at a low mix; Amount brings them up, Chaos scatters the grains and reverses more.
Desert Twang: Harmonic tremolo, a bright clean amp, an open-back cabinet, drippy spring and a short echo for twangy guitar; Amount adds wobble and space, Drive pushes the amp.
Wall of Sound: Blended fuzz, a thick chorus and a big hall with a spectral freeze ready to hold the sound; Amount adds fuzz and wash, Size grows the hall.
Mutant Space: A modulated reverb with an octave-up shift and a slowly drifting ring modulator; Amount adds reverb, Mutate brings in the pitch and the ring.
Pop Vocal: De-plosive, de-esser, compression, a polished EQ, light doubling and a plate for modern pop vocals; Amount compresses harder, Space adds doubling and plate.
Rap Vocal Upfront: Gate, fast FET compression, tube drive, de-essing and a short ducked eighth echo for upfront rap vocals; Amount compresses harder, Echo adds more delay.
Airy Ballad: Smooth opto compression, sparkle, a ducked ping-pong delay and a shimmer for soft ballad vocals; Amount adds delay and shimmer, Air brightens.
Choir Pad Vocal: A fifth above and an octave below, a deeper formant, a wide chorus and a shimmer turn one voice into a choir pad; Amount brings up the voices, Voice deepens them.
Podcast Ready: Noise reduction, hum removal, de-plosive, de-esser, leveling and a limiter, with a meter set to -16 LUFS; Amount cleans harder, Loudness raises the level.
Snare Crack: More attack, a cracking EQ, tape drive and a short room for snares; Amount adds attack and drive, Room adds the room.
Hat Shine: High-pass, sparkle, shorter tails and extra width for hi-hats and cymbals; Amount adds shine and tightens, Width spreads them.
808 Glue: A sub octave, tube drive, a soft clipper and mono lows to glue an 808; Amount drives and clips harder, Sub adds more sub.
Reese Bass: Mono lows, with tube drive, a wide chorus and a slowly moving phaser above them for reese and synth bass; Amount drives and thickens, Motion adds the phaser.
Low End Focus: Mono lows, a dynamic cut on boom around 100 Hz and a touch of sub, all on the low band only; Amount cuts the boom more, Sub adds sub.
Ambient Guitar: Softened attacks, a modulated dotted-quarter ping-pong and a long shimmer for ambient guitar; Amount adds echo and shimmer, Swell softens the picking more.
Classic Wah Rig: An envelope wah into a crunchy amp, 2x12 cabinet and spring; Amount makes the wah deeper, Drive pushes the amp.
Jet Flange: A tempo-synced, high-feedback flanger sweep into tape warmth; Amount makes the jet stronger, Manual shifts where the sweep sits.
Frozen Hall: A wide, modulated hall with long pre-delay and a gentle top roll-off; Amount adds hall, Freeze holds the tail.
Loud Master: Slight tilt, gentle multiband compression, a soft clipper and a maximizer, with a loudness meter at the end; Amount pushes louder, Bright tilts brighter.
Channel Strip: Gate, a clean-up EQ, bus compression, de-essing and tape color in a classic console order; Amount compresses harder, Color adds drive.
Pultec Lift: A low shelf boost with a wide cut above it, a broad high lift, a soft 20 kHz shelf down and tube color; Amount boosts more, Warmth adds drive.
Abbey Chamber: A plate with long pre-delay and the low and high end cut from the reverb only, plus light tape, like a classic echo chamber; Amount adds chamber, Length lengthens it.
Sub Harmonics: An octave down, a sub layer and mono, all below 120 Hz, to add weight; Amount adds both, Depth adds a second octave down.
Pusher: Attack, sparkle, width and a soft clipper to push a sound forward; Amount does more of all of it, Width spreads it.
Stutter Build: Sixteenth repeats on the second half of each bar, a rising high-pass and a wash, all on one control for a build-up; a second control makes the repeats shorter.
Dub Echo Bus: A dark multi-head tape echo with its spring, a low cut and more spring for dub; Amount adds echo and repeats, Wobble adds tape wow and flutter.
Ambient Wash: A shimmering reverb into drifting grains and a vast detuned space, for pads and evolving textures.
Drum Replace: Each hit of a recorded kick plays the Drum Machine's kick instead, with the hit's own dynamics.
Phone Vocal: A telephone voice with a little grit and a short slap echo.
Transient Verb: Reverb on the tail of each sound only, so the attack stays dry and close.
